title: Three Winters and One Short Jest
subtitle: 人际交往 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际交往（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通）
meta: 主题语境：人际交往（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通）　|　核心词汇：fool　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fool 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 the teacher ① pitied a fool that no neighbour in the street would have named, and he said the pitying was the whole of the winter. The ② fool, meaning the man himself and not the jest, ran three winters and stayed unnamed in the book; a fool, he said, is the only thing in a street that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ fool in that street had the same short jest beside him, and the ④ fool at the far table, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A fool, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; the teacher said the naming is the part that fills three winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the fool was the whole of the matter, meaning the jester and not the man. The ⑥ fool, meaning the jester and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody names; fool, he said, is either somebody you pity or the only word that means both a simple man and a jester. He said the jester is the part they remember.

By 1970 the ⑦ fool had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short jest. The ⑧ fool of the whole thing, the teacher wrote in January, was one street and three winters of naming; fool, he said, is either the one at the far table or the reason you learned to name. He said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ fool I remember is the one named in the plan, which closed in 1972 and is still described as the quietest in the street. A ⑩ fool, my mother said in 1974, is the only one that improves by being named; every fool, she said, is a jester that has agreed to look like a man. She said the jester was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 傻瓜；蠢人（指街上每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 傻瓜（指那一个本身，与玩笑相对）
C. 固定搭配：pity a fool 怜悯一个傻瓜
D. n. 傻瓜（指留给孩子们的那一类）
E. n. 傻瓜（抽象总称，指一条街上的痴愚之事）
F. n. 傻瓜（指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一个）
G. n. 弄臣；小丑（旧时宫廷中供人取笑者，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样人）
H. n. 弄臣（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说破的那样人）

items.q: pitied a fool that no neighbour in the street would have named
The fool, meaning the man himself and not the jest
the fool at the far table
the fool was the whole of the matter
the fool had become a line in a plan
The fool of the whole thing
A fool, my mother said in 1974

answers.why: pity a fool 意为“怜悯一个傻瓜”，1963 年那位先生怜悯了一个街上没有一位邻居肯说出名字的傻瓜。
fool 意为“傻瓜”，指那一个本身而不是玩笑，他经过了三个冬天而在簿子上没有被说出名字。
fool 意为“傻瓜”，指街上每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一个短短的笑话。
fool 意为“傻瓜”，指留给孩子们的那一类，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
fool 意为“弄臣、小丑”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样人，叔叔说那个弄臣就是那件事的全部。
fool 意为“弄臣”，指人人都等却无人说破的那样人而不是那个傻瓜，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的人。
fool 意为“傻瓜”，指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一个，到 1970 年这一个成了计划里的一行。
fool 意为“傻瓜”，那位先生一月写道，整件事的痴愚之事是一条街道和三个冬天的说出名字。
fool 意为“傻瓜”，我记得的是计划里被说出名字的那一个，1972 年结束了，至今仍被说成街上最安静的一个。
fool 为抽象总称，母亲 1974 年说，一个傻瓜是唯一会因为被好好说出名字而变得更好的人。
